$comment: The proof section on the landing page — the rail of clients, the globe they sit on,
and the quote that rotates beside it.
Both lists start empty on purpose: an empty list renders a placeholder that says so,
and nothing invented ships in the meantime. Fill them in and the placeholders go away.
clients[]      id     a short slug, unique. Letters, digits and dashes.
name   the wordmark on the rail, and the label on the globe.
lat    latitude, -90 to 90 (north is positive).
lng    longitude, -180 to 180 (east is positive).
e.g. Buenos Aires is lat -34.6, lng -58.4.
logo   optional. A path under public/, e.g. "/logos/casa-lima.svg".
Without one the rail sets the name as a wordmark, which is the
right answer for a client who has no mark worth reproducing.
The rail repeats a short list until it is wider than the screen, so
three clients loop without a gap. Six or more stop repeating.
testimonials[] quote  what they said, in the language they said it in — a real quote
is published in its own words, so this is not translated.
role   the business and what they do: «Tienda de indumentaria · 2 locales».
name   optional. Leave it out for a customer who agreed to be quoted but
not named — the role stands as the attribution on its own.
avatar optional. A path under public/, e.g. "/people/lucia.jpg".
Without one the card sets initials on the same plate the app uses
for a contact with no photo.
One quote is on screen at a time and they rotate. Two is enough for that
to be a rotation; below that the card just holds the one it has.

testimonials.quote: Pasamos de responder en horas a responder en minutos. El bot resuelve lo repetitivo y nosotros cerramos la venta.
testimonials.name: Lucía Fernández

testimonials.quote: Centralizamos WhatsApp e Instagram en un solo lugar. Con la base de conocimiento el agente contesta solo lo que sabe.
